title: Advanced Type Inference knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Advanced Type Inference”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Kotlin infers a declaration’s type from its initializer when it can do so, while an explicit type annotation can clarify an API or a tricky expression.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: Kotlin infers a declaration’s type from its initializer when it can do so, while an explicit type annotation can clarify an API or a tricky expression.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Kotlin infers a declaration’s type from its initializer when it can do so, while an explicit type annotation can clarify an API or a tricky expression. questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Advanced Type Inference”?
options: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Advanced Type Inference”?
options: Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Advanced Type Inference removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.answer_key: Advanced Type Inference removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Advanced Type Inference removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
